Channelization is provided at such intersections as is warranted. Left-turn lanes are regularly provided, and in some cases, right-turn lanes.
Also included in this project are two (2) pedestrian overpasses and a railroad grade separation structure.
An additional Federal action in the area of this proposed improvement is concerned with the Illinois Central Gulf Railroad Commuter Station, located in the northeast quadrant of the intersection between Lincoln Highway and Olympian Way in the Village of Olympia Fields, Illinois. A Negative Declaration was prepared for this project dated April 1973 and titled 211th Street Commuter Parking Facility; 23-1, 23-2 VB; Cook County, Illinois. The Negative Declaration was concurred with and signed by the District Engineer of the Federal Highway Administration on August 7, 1973.
IV. SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS AND ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS
A. Displacement of People
Every effort was made in the planning of the project to minimize the right-of-way requirements. However, a total of eight (8) structures will be affected by total acquisition in order to implement this proposal. Other buildings will be affected to the extent that overhangs will have to be removed or modified.
A total of six (6) commercial structures will be directly effected because of the highway reconstruction and widening. Of the six (6) buildings, five are highway oriented drive-in restaurants and one is an office structure.
Two residential structures will need to be acquired for rightof-way purposes. One of these structures is a single family house and the other is an apartment building with sixteen single family units.
B. Significant Noise Impacts
The noise pollution impact caused by the improvement of this route was determined by comparison of existing (1973) noise levels, predicted (1990) noise levels and design year noise level standards. From this comparison for each of the buildings or sites judged as having the highest probability of noise susceptibility in relation to the proposed improvement, it was determined that this project will have a design year noise impact. The predicted traffic-generated L10 noise levels for the design year are higher than the design year standards contained in PPM 90-2 for Land Use Categories "B", "C" and "E".
